payload.claim: `_record_for` caches one `RefsRecord` per mirror path and now bakes that task's `origin` into the cached instance at construction time. `RoutedRecord.append` (line 37) then discards the freshly-resolved `origin` from `_record_for` and relies on the cached object's stored `_origin` for `RefsRecord._adopt`'s fetch. Since `mirror_path` is a digest of the local checkout path alone, not of the origin URL (`saffron/cli.py:1999`), two different `repos` rows (different origins) can share one mirror path if a checkout directory is ever reused for a different origin; whichever origin was first resolved for that mirror stays cached and is used as every later task's fetch source on that mirror, even when that later task's true origin differs. `RoutedRecord.push` avoids this by re-resolving `origin` fresh on every call and passing it explicitly; `append` does not, so it is the one path that can silently fetch from (or wrongly fail against) the wrong remote on an origin-reused-mirror-path collision.
